sections.h2: How does selling a house in Dublin, Ohio work?
sections.html:
A Dublin seller can list through an agent, sell without one, or take a cash purchase, and the first step is learning which county holds your parcel. Dublin is a Columbus suburb whose boundaries fall within Franklin, Delaware, Union and Madison counties, so deed transfer, valuation and recording depend on the county of record. The Census Bureau counted 49,328 residents in 2020 and estimates 49,094 for July 2025, with 24.44 square miles of land.

The Scioto River runs through the city and cuts gorges into limestone bedrock, which leaves ravines and a few steep cliffs on otherwise flat ground. The city sits on the Glaciated Allegheny Plateau, with elevations from 780 feet where the river leaves the city to about 1,000 feet at Glacier Ridge Metro Park.

sections.h2: How did Dublin grow so quickly?
sections.html:
Dublin went from 681 residents in 1970 to 3,855 in 1980 and 16,366 in 1990, a shift tied to the construction of Interstate 270 and the arrival of corporate headquarters. It was declared a city in August 1987 after passing 5,000 residents. By 2000 the count was 31,392, and by 2020 it reached 49,328.

The name comes from John Shields, an Irishman who partnered with John Sells to survey lots for the village around 1810 and named it after Dublin, Ireland. The Dublin Irish Festival, billed as the largest three-day Irish festival in the world, is held here, and the Memorial Tournament has been played at Muirfield Village Golf Club since 1976.

Since 2020 the city has been redeveloping the Bridge Street District, a 1,100-acre project along the Scioto River with apartments, condominiums, retail and offices. The project includes about 400 apartments and condominiums.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Dublin housing?
sections.html:
Dublin's values and owner rate are both high. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts for 2020 through 2024 show the following.

  • Median value of owner-occupied housing: $563,500.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 77.1 percent, across 17,995 households averaging 2.72 people.
  • Median gross rent: $1,686; median owner cost with a mortgage: $3,055, and $1,349 without one.
  • Median household income: $160,296; bachelor's degree or higher among adults 25 and older: 73.4 percent.
  • Residents living in the same house a year earlier: 92.7 percent; foreign-born residents: 20.5 percent.

A 92.7 percent same-house rate means few households moved into or within the city in the prior year.

sections.h2: Which employers and roads link Dublin to Columbus?
sections.html:
The city is home to the headquarters of Cardinal Health, Wendy's, OCLC, IGS Energy and Stanley Steemer. Wikipedia, citing the city's 2020 financial report, lists the largest local employers as Cardinal Health (4,800), OhioHealth (2,000), Dublin City School District (1,951), CareWorks (1,622), OCLC (750) and Wendy's (725). OhioHealth's Dublin Methodist Hospital is among its operations here.

Interstate 270, called the Outerbelt, and State Route 161 are the main expressways. U.S. Route 33 runs together with Route 161 between the roundabout in the center of Dublin and an interchange near an Ohio University satellite campus. State Routes 257 and 745 run along each side of the Scioto River. The Dublin Link, a pedestrian and cycling bridge, opened in March 2020. COTA runs route 33 to downtown Dublin and the Bridge Street District and an express route 73 at rush hour.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Dublin houses?
sections.html:
The Dublin City School District serves the city, and the Hilliard City School District serves a portion of it. Dublin City has three high schools (Coffman, Scioto and Jerome), five middle schools (Sells, Davis, Grizzell, Karrer and Eversole) and fifteen elementary schools. Enrollment for the 2020 to 2021 school year was 16,254.

Hilliard runs Washington Elementary School inside Dublin's limits. A listing that names a school should check the attendance area for that parcel, because the attendance boundary rather than the city name determines the school.

sections.h2: What permits does Dublin require for house work before a sale?
sections.html:
Dublin processes residential permit applications online through its Accela Citizen Access portal and an electronic plan review system. The city treats residential projects as those on property with one, two or three family dwelling units. Its list of projects that need permits includes the following.

  • New homes and additions.
  • Interior remodeling, including basement remodels.
  • Decks and porches.
  • Swimming pools and hot tubs.

Permits must be paid for and issued before work starts, and electrical, HVAC and plumbing contractors must be registered where registration is required. The state of Ohio adds a 1 percent surcharge to residential fees other than plumbing and sewer or water fees. If a remodel in your house was done without a permit, ask the city's Building Standards office what it takes to close it out before a buyer's inspection.

sections.h2: What are Dublin's rules on code enforcement and deed restrictions?
sections.html:
Dublin enforces zoning, health, parking, nuisance and sign codes, and it says most violation notices allow ten days to comply, with more time possible in unusual circumstances. A complaint is investigated first, and no action follows if no violation is found. Code Enforcement can be reached at 614.410.4600.

The city separates zoning from private deed restrictions and says it does not generally have standing to enforce a deed restriction. Many Dublin subdivisions have restrictions enforced by an association, so a seller with an association should gather the governing documents and any unpaid dues before listing, since buyers will ask.

sections.h2: Can I rent out a Dublin house short term before selling?
sections.html:
Only on tight terms, and only with a city registration. Dublin's short-term rental ordinance, passed on October 12, 2020, took effect for operators as of November 11, 2020. The city lists its main features below.

Dublin short-term rental rules as listed by the city (source: Code Compliance and Enforcement page)
RuleWhat the city lists
RegistrationAnnual registration required before listing
Annual fee$225, valid through December 31 of the approval year
Rental limitTwo weeks per calendar year, in up to two increments of seven days
First-offense fine$250 for operating without registering
Primary residence proofTwo of five listed documents, such as a driver's license or utility bill

The city also requires insurance verification, a notarized affidavit of compliance and a form submitted before each rental period. The registration number must be posted with any listing.

sections.h2: What county costs apply to a Dublin deed, and what does Ohio require?
sections.html:
For the Delaware County portion of Dublin, the Recorder's fee page lists $39 for the first two pages of a deed, including a $5 preservation surcharge, and $8 for each additional page. The Auditor's forms page carries the Real Property Conveyance Fee Statement, form DTE 100, and the Auditor's 2026 triennial valuation page lists a complaint window running from January 1, 2027, through March 31, 2027, for the Delaware County values. Parcels in Franklin or Union County follow those counties' offices, so ask the county auditor and recorder for the current figures.

Ohio's property disclosure law, R.C. 5302.30, makes the owner of a home with one to four units complete the state form for the buyer. When the buyer gets it late, after contracting, cancellation in writing is open for three business days from receipt and closes by the earlier of thirty days from acceptance or the closing date.

faqs.q: Which county do I deal with when I sell a house in Dublin?
faqs.a: It depends on the parcel. Dublin falls within Franklin, Delaware, Union and Madison counties, so check your tax bill or the county auditor's property search to see which office records your deed.

faqs.q: Can I list my Dublin house on Airbnb to cover the mortgage while it sells?
faqs.a: Only with a city registration and within tight limits. The city allows two weeks per calendar year, charges $225 for annual registration, and lists a $250 fine for operating without registering.

faqs.q: How long do I have to fix a Dublin code violation?
faqs.a: Most notices give ten days, and the city says code enforcement staff can discuss and extend that time when circumstances are unusual. You can call Code Enforcement at 614.410.4600.

faqs.q: Does the city enforce my neighborhood's deed restrictions?
faqs.a: Generally not. The city says it does not have standing to pursue enforcement of deed restrictions, so those fall to an association or neighbors. City zoning rules are separate.

faqs.q: What is Dublin's median home value?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists a median value of $563,500 for owner-occupied homes in Dublin for 2020 through 2024, with an owner-occupied rate of 77.1 percent.
